Senses.Explanation: Gave a shout is the records' stock narrative formula for one performed vocal move in a public interview or teaching-seat event. Muzhou Daoming uses it after an unnamed monk shouts at him, asks what comes after three or four shouts, and strikes when no words follow. Feiyin Tongrong shouts amid a high-seat address and says that without stopping the entangling talk with a shout it would nearly have gone on without end (若不喝住，幾乎打葛藤無有了時也). Nanyue Falun Qitian performs four shouts in sequence and labels them respectively “the lion roars,” “the elephant king stretches,” “a mad dog chases a clod,” and “a shrimp cannot leap out of the dipper”; these are four stated comparisons, not four senses. Elsewhere an unnamed monk shouts and exits, Yunfu Zhi shouts before ascending the formal seat and offering incense, and Feiyin shouts before returning to the abbot's quarters. The same formula can close an address, combine with planting the staff, or precede questions to the assembly. Chan records preserve the shout as a positioned public move; the entry reports that position and any stated classification without assigning it an unstated force.
Senses.Note: The formula occurs 7,091 times in 320 allowlisted texts. In the word family, “shout” can be a noun or verb, “one shout” counts it, and “gave a shout” is the finite narrative action. Speaker, addressee, and sequence position are different deployments of the same action, not different things. Comparison frames include leaving the seat, ascending the seat, planting the staff, and returning to the abbot's quarters.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin (費隱禪師語錄): Feiyin Tongrong describes his performed shout as stopping an otherwise endless stretch of entangling talk, then asks how to state a line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂拈袈裟角，云：大眾！人人有分，須是頂門眼開始得。喝一喝，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Ancestral Guidelines (列祖提綱錄): the anthology explicitly introduces Zhenjing Kewen, who lifts a corner of his robe, tells the assembly that everyone has a share but must open the crown eye, gives one shout, and leaves the seat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 良久，云：向下文長，付在來日。喝一喝。良久，云：無為無事人，猶是金鎖難。喝一喝，卓拄杖，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials of Continued Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (續古尊宿語要): Ciming Chuyuan performs two shouts in the address; the second combines with planting the staff and leaving the seat.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄): the explicit Yungai Zhiyong heading governs the exchange and address; Yungai Zhiyong surveys the assembly, shouts once, and asks whether they take this as host and guest distinctly evident.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄): the explicit Nanyue Falun Qitian heading governs the address; Nanyue Falun Qitian gives four successive shouts and labels their displayed comparisons.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄): after Poshan Haiming strikes him twice, the unnamed monk gives one shout and leaves; Poshan then rests. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not give a personal name for the unnamed monk.
Recorded Sayings of Yunfu Zhi (雲腹智禪師語錄): at his Wudeng Monastery opening, Yunfu Zhi shouts once and immediately ascends the seat for the incense offering.
Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Feiyin Tongrong gives one shout and returns to the abbot's quarters.
